C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT.IntentSummary: Split release.yml's privileged build job into an unsigned build job and a separate sign job so dependency install scripts and Vite build plugins never execute in a job holding signing material: the build job loses environment: release-signing, id-token: write, attestations: write and every secrets.* reference, runs npm ci --ignore-scripts with exactly one allowlisted install-script entry (esbuild, the only hasInstallScript package this change allows, matching the authorize-tag :182 precedent), stages UNSIGNED bundles with a SHA-256 receipt per staged artifact reusing the existing .sha256 sidecar machinery, and keeps every gate that works on an unsigned bundle (repeated stable-lane admission, materials, preflight, typecheck, warnings allowlist, attributions, SBOM, unsigned-capable smoke per the release-tauri.yml ad-hoc precedent); a new sign job, needs-chained on build, is the only holder of the release-signing environment, the APPLE_*/TAURI_SIGNING_* secrets and the OIDC attestation authority — it downloads the build's artifacts, recomputes every digest against the recorded receipts and refuses the run on any mismatch before any signing step, then performs the Apple import/codesign/notarize/staple flow by re-signing the staged unsigned bundle and repackaging (never rebuilding — the tauri-action build+sign coupling is named, the sign-staged-bundle approach is the plan, rebuild-in-sign is out of bounds), signs the Tauri updater archives for both platform sets, recomposes the latest-platform.json fragments byte-identically with signatures produced here, and hosts the moved SLSA provenance and keyless cosign steps so they attest the signed release set; prepare-publication's needs list gains sign explicitly so no downstream stage bypasses signing. The trust model is needs-chain plus digest comparison against the build's receipts — no node_modules handoff, no cross-run trust. tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js lands the boundary-guard pins FIRST as T-001 freezing today's boundary (secrets only in the build job's two tauri steps, id-token: write in no job except build, manual-build and docs-security secret-free and environment-free), then each workflow-editing task consciously updates the affected pins with red controls; the prerelease lane and the C-RELEASE-BETA-CHECKS-GATE boundary stay byte-compatible in behavior; docs/release-process.md gains a signing section describing the unsigned-build/digest-verified-sign flow and the allowlist; release.yml's own GRACE markup, the M-046 SummaryDelta and V-M-046 are synchronized.

T-001.Title: Boundary-guard source pins FIRST: freeze today's pre-split signing boundary in the governance test before any release.yml edit

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Extend tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js inside START_BLOCK_RELEASE_GOVERNANCE_TESTS, keeping every existing test unweakened (the beta-checks-gate pins, the gitleaks checksum contract and the stable-lane pins all keep passing). Derive a buildJob slice and a sign-job-absence observation in the file's existing split style (buildJob splits the checked-in release.yml on the /^ prepare-publication:/m boundary so it ends at the next top-level job key), plus a manualBuildJob slice splitting on /^ build:/m, and pin TODAY's pre-split boundary exactly: the build job source declares environment: release-signing, carries id-token: write and attestations: write in its permissions block, and the only secrets.* references inside it are the two tauri-action steps' env blocks — TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY(_PASSWORD) on both platforms (:517-518, :532-533) and the seven APPLE_* entries on macOS only (:519-524); no step outside those two tauri steps in the build job references secrets.*; id-token: write and attestations: write exist in no other job of release.yml (authorize-tag keeps contents: read + checks: read, manual-build only contents: read, prepare-publication only contents: read, publish contents: write without id-token, publish-cask unchanged); manual-build and the governance workflow's docs-security job carry no secrets.* reference and no environment: declaration; the build job's install step is plain run: npm ci (:472-473) while authorize-tag keeps run: npm ci --ignore-scripts (:182); package-lock.json still marks esbuild hasInstallScript: true. A comment in the test names the finding by key (release-build-scripts-share-signing-job) and records that these pins freeze the pre-split boundary so the split's widening is a conscious, reviewed update to a green pin rather than unnoticed drift.

Add the comment-blind red-control validator assertReleaseSigningSplit(source, opts) mirroring the file's assertGitleaksChecksumContract/assertPrereleaseChecksGate precedent: it mutates only the in-memory source string (no network, no tracked-file edits) and rejects, each with a distinct expectation — a secrets.* reference appearing in any non-tauri build step; an id-token: write or attestations: write permission outside the designated holder job; a secrets.* reference or environment: declaration in manual-build or docs-security; and an npm ci in the designated holder job that lacks --ignore-scripts once the split lands (parameterized so the same validator drives both today's boundary via T-001's pins and the post-split boundary via the later tasks' updated pins, without weakening any control between states).

Synchronize the test file's local markup only: VERSION 2.3.0 to 2.4.0 and a dated 2026-11-22 CHANGE_SUMMARY entry for C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT describing the boundary-guard freeze. No edit to .github/workflows/release.yml or any other file — this task exists so the guard is green on the untouched workflow before T-002 touches it. Documentation comments are not mixed with secrets, pins or job-condition changes here because there are none: this task edits only the test file.

T-002.Title: Build-job hardening: ignore-scripts install with the single esbuild allowlist entry, environment/id-token/secrets removal, and unsigned bundle staging with per-artifact SHA-256 receipts

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Replace the build job's plain npm ci (:472-473) with run: npm ci --ignore-scripts followed by exactly one allowlisted script step that runs node node_modules/esbuild/install.js, preceded by a comment recording that esbuild is the single approved install-script exception (esbuild) — the only hasInstallScript package this change allows, matching the authorize-tag :182 precedent — and that any future entry requires a reviewed change; no second allowlist entry, no lifecycle scripts for platform packages, and the sign job must not run a plain npm ci either when it lands in T-003. The exact phrase "single approved install-script exception (esbuild)" appears in the workflow comment. Update T-001's guard pins for this install shape in the same task: the build-slice pin asserting plain npm ci becomes a pin asserting npm ci --ignore-scripts plus the single esbuild entry, with red controls rejecting a plain npm ci in the build slice, a second allowlisted script, or an allowlisted script for anything but esbuild.

Strip the signing material from the build job: delete the environment: release-signing declaration (:387) and the id-token: write and attestations: write permissions (:391-392) so build keeps exactly contents: read and checks: read; remove the env secrets from both tauri-action steps so they build UNSIGNED bundles (the macOS step loses the TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY(_PASSWORD) and seven APPLE_* entries, the Windows step its TAURI entries), rename them to state the unsigned output, and remove the now-unapplicable "verify signed and notarized app" step (:537-547) from build — Developer ID codesign/spctl verification moves to the sign job in T-003. Adapt the macOS smoke, bundle-size, warnings-allowlist, attributions and SBOM gates to the unsigned bundle without weakening any assertion that still applies (the smoke follows the release-tauri.yml ad-hoc precedent of :136-156 for launching an unsigned/ad-hoc-signed app; host-behavior proof stays with the live CI run, never asserted from local reasoning). Update T-001's guard pins in the same task: environment/id-token/secrets move from "in build" to "in no job yet except via the not-yet-existing sign job" — the conscious, reviewed widening the guard exists to force; red controls keep rejecting a secrets.*/id-token reappearance anywhere outside the single designated holder.

Make the staging steps record a SHA-256 receipt for EVERY staged artifact, extending the existing sidecar machinery — the macOS stage (:703-731) already writes the DMG sidecar via shasum -a 256 (:721) and gains receipts for the updater archive, SBOMs and notices; the Windows stage (:846-869) already hashes the installer (:865-868) and gains receipts for its remaining staged files — and the uploads (:935-960) carry the receipts so the sign job can verify the complete staged set. The artifact names mark-${{ matrix.platform.name }}-release stay unchanged. Synchronize release.yml's own GRACE markup in this task: VERSION 3.8.0 to 3.9.0, the MODULE_MAP build entry rewritten for the unsigned boundary (C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT named: unsigned build, receipts, no signing material), and a dated 2026-11-22 CHANGE_SUMMARY entry naming C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT and the build-job hardening; MODULE_CONTRACT and all other markup stay as-is. Keep every other byte of behavior: no new job in this task, no change to triggers, concurrency, the workflow-level permissions block, authorize-tag (the C-RELEASE-BETA-CHECKS-GATE steps and conditions byte-identical), manual-build, publish or publish-cask; the stable-lane-only skips (download admitted check evidence, repeat strict admission, materials, preflight — all if: needs.authorize-tag.outputs.prerelease != 'true') keep their exact conditions and bytes; the updater feed fragment steps keep their graceful skip when signatures are absent (their signed composition moves to the sign job in T-003).

T-003.Title: New sign job: digest verification, Apple re-sign/notarize/staple, Tauri updater signing, SLSA provenance and keyless cosign

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add a new sign job to .github/workflows/release.yml (needs: [authorize-tag, build], strategy matrix mirroring the build job's platform set) that is the sole holder of the signing material: environment: release-signing, permissions id-token: write and attestations: write (the only job carrying either), and the APPLE_*/TAURI_* secrets exclusively in its steps. Its first step downloads the staged unsigned artifacts (actions/download-artifact) and verifies EVERY staged file against the build job's recorded SHA-256 receipts — a mismatch, a missing receipt or an unexpected extra staged file fails the job with the marker [ReleaseSign][sign][BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH] before any secret is touched; the verification compares recomputed shasum -a 256 digests against the receipts uploaded by T-002 and treats an absent receipt file itself as a failure. The macOS lane then re-signs the staged unsigned bundle without rebuilding: Apple certificate import from base64 secrets, codesign of the .app inside the staged .dmg bundle (or the staged .app artifact) with theDeveloper ID identity, notarization via notarytool with APPLE_ID/PASSWORD/TEAM_ID, staple, and the Developer ID codesign/spctl verification moved here from the old build step (:537-547); tauri-action's build+sign coupling is deliberately NOT used here — the plan signs the staged bundle, rebuild-in-sign is out of bounds. The Windows lane applies the Tauri updater signing to the staged unsigned installer/bundle with TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY(_PASSWORD). The SLSA provenance (actions/attest-build-provenance) and keyless cosign sign-blob steps (:879-933) move from the build job into the sign job unchanged in effect, now attesting the signed artifacts. The signed set uploads under the unchanged artifact names mark-${{ matrix.platform.name }}-release so downstream consumers see the same names as today. The build job keeps no environment, no id-token, no secrets — pins for this land in T-005.

T-004.Title: The sign job: digest verification before any signing, Apple re-sign/repackage/notarize/staple of the staged bundle, Tauri updater signing, SLSA and keyless cosign moved here

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add a new sign job with a matrix mirroring build's two platforms (macos-15 aarch64-apple-darwin, windows-latest x86_64-pc-windows-msvc), needs: build, the same push-and-authorize-tag-success condition shape as build, environment: release-signing (the only job carrying it — the attachment point moves from build to sign; the environment's definition, reviewers and tag restriction are untouched), and permissions exactly contents: read, checks: read, id-token: write, attestations: write — the only place id-token: write and attestations: write exist in the workflow. APPLE_* and TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY(_PASSWORD) secrets are referenced only in this job. The MODULE_MAP gains a sign entry whose description contains the exact phrase "signs digest-verified staged artifacts without rebuilding".

The sign job's FIRST steps download the build job's mark-${{ matrix.platform.name }}-release artifacts and run a step named "verify staged artifact digests" that recomputes each staged artifact's SHA-256 against its recorded receipt and exits nonzero on any mismatch BEFORE any signing step, with ::error:: lines prefixed [ReleaseSign][sign][BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH] naming the offending artifact and both digests, and no status-swallowing construct around the comparison (no || true, no if-without-exit). The exact step name and marker are pinned in the governance test with red controls rejecting a sign job that signs before verifying, that swallows the mismatch exit, or that lacks the verification step. Only after verification pass do the signing steps run: on macOS, the tauri-action build+sign coupling is the named constraint — this change does NOT rebuild in the sign job (a silent fallback to rebuild-in-sign is out of bounds); the job re-signs the digest-verified staged .app (cert import from APPLE_CERTIFICATE, codesign with APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY), repackages the DMG and updater archive from the signed .app, submits to Apple notary and staples (notarytool/stapler via APPLE_ID/PASSWORD/TEAM_ID), then runs the Developer ID codesign/spctl verification moved from :537-547; on both platforms the Tauri updater signing (TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY(_PASSWORD)) produces the .sig files and the latest-platform.json fragments are recomposed here byte-identically to the current composition (:686-695, :833-842) with signatures produced in this job. Which repackage mechanism proves out is recorded with the first live CI run; if a detail defeats the sign-staged-bundle approach, the resolution is an owner-visible decision in the change bundle, not a rebuild.

Move the SLSA build-provenance steps (:879-889) and the cosign keyless sign-blob steps (:900-933) verbatim-in-shape from build into the sign job so provenance and keyless signatures attest the signed release set, and re-emit fresh .sha256 receipts for every artifact the sign job repackaged or signed (the asset inventory names prepare-publication consumes — Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg, .dmg.sha256, .dmg.bundle, .app.tar.gz, latest.json and the Windows set — stay exactly as today). Upload the signed set under the same mark-${{ matrix.platform.name }}-release artifact names for the downstream publication chain. Update the guard pins for the post-split shape in the same task: sign is the sole holder of environment/id-token/attestations/secrets with verify-then-sign ordering; build is free of all four. Keep every other byte of behavior: the prerelease lane needs no sign-side condition (prerelease and stable tags flow through the same split chain), authorize-tag stays byte-identical, no new secrets, no new workflow file, and the sign job declares no permission beyond the four above.

T-005.Title: Needs-chain rewiring: publication strictly downstream of signing, with prerelease-lane equivalence pins

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Change prepare-publication's needs from [authorize-tag, build] (:964) to needs: [authorize-tag, build, sign]; publish keeps needs: [authorize-tag, build, prepare-publication] (:1125) unchanged so every publication path is transitively downstream of signing; publish keeps its release environment with contents: write (:1134-1137), its conditions, concurrency, tag triggers and the workflow-level permissions block byte-identical; prepare-publication continues reading needs.build.outputs.tag and consuming the same artifact names (its steps byte-identical except the needs line). The governance test pins the chain: sign needs build, prepare-publication's needs include sign, and no stage between build and prepare-publication bypasses sign — with a red control rejecting a needs list that drops sign.

Pin prerelease-lane equivalence explicitly: prerelease and stable tags flow through the same split build-to-sign chain; the prerelease-only skips (download admitted evidence, repeated strict admission, materials, preflight, identity artifact) keep their exact if: needs.authorize-tag.outputs.prerelease != 'true' conditions on build, where they live after the split; authorize-tag's C-RELEASE-BETA-CHECKS-GATE collection/gate steps and conditions are byte-identical (the existing prerelease pins in the test file keep passing unweakened); publish-cask's skip and publish's prerelease branch are untouched; the stable lane's admission, publication and cask semantics are unchanged. Red controls reject any new prerelease-condition divergence introduced by the split (a sign job conditioned on prerelease either way beyond the build-mirroring condition, or a moved skip condition).

Update the remaining guard pins to the final post-split boundary in the same task (the full widening now complete and reviewed): the whole-file assertions — id-token: write in exactly one job, environment: release-signing in exactly one job, APPLE_*/TAURI_* secrets in exactly one job, the old needs: [authorize-tag, build] string absent — plus the chain and equivalence pins of the two criteria above. No docs or graph/verification edits in this task: documentation is never mixed with secrets, pins or job-condition changes in the same task.
